source.title: Gradient constrained sharpness-aware prompt learning for vision-language models
source.authors: Liangchen Liu; Nannan Wang; Da-Wei Zhou; Xin-Bo Gao; Decheng Liu; Xi Yang; Tong-Liang Liu

record.file_problem: none; the complete paper text and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests sharpness-aware prompt learning in a new setting: seen-to-unseen class generalization in CLIP. Its seen/unseen class results do not test the claim's same-distribution train/test gap or arbitrary-label memorization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports prompt-learning results on seen and unseen classes and relates them to loss value and loss sharpness. These class-split results are a related but different generalization construct; no claim version is directly tested.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization relationship to design prompt optimization for frozen CLIP. Its results measure seen/unseen class transfer and domain transfer, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train/test gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that jointly accounting for loss value and sharpness through gradient constraints improves the seen/unseen performance trade-off in prompt learning.
record.recipe_differences: Prompt learning adapts frozen CLIP using a small set of tunable text-token vectors and evaluates disjoint seen and unseen classes; it does not test arbitrary-label memorization or same-distribution train/test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation radius and gradient constraint thresholds affect seen and unseen class performance; the paper reports dataset-specific hyperparameter adjustments.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 11 datasets, CoOp, SCoOp and GCSCoOp achieve average seen/unseen accuracies of 82.68/64.15%, 79.29/72.52% and 82.46/73.95%, respectively. Loss-landscape visualizations associate flatter prompt minima with transfer performance, while emphasizing differences in converged loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In few-shot frozen-CLIP prompt learning, gradient-constrained SAM improves unseen-class transfer while largely preserving CoOp's seen-class accuracy; vanilla SAM incurs a larger seen-class penalty.

record.problems: The reported benchmark averages are over three random seeds, but no uncertainty estimates are stated. The evaluation uses a seen/unseen class split rather than the claim's same-distribution train/test split, and does not test random-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows selected. The paper also reports per-dataset results and cross-domain evaluations in Tables 1, 2 and 5 and Appendix tables; these address prompt-learning class/domain transfer rather than any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus random-label training fit and held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train/test generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3/tests classification conflicts with its correct assessment that no version is directly tested. Table 1 improvements are percentage-point differences: GCSCoOp gains 9.80 points on unseen classes and loses 0.22 points on seen classes versus CoOp. Related transfer and landscape results do not establish a verdict on V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels under the same training recipe.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error on the same distribution.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers trained from scratch.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the stated tuning conditions.
Large- versus small-batch train/test generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on held-out error under the specified training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and train/test gaps among networks with similarly low training loss; the paper instead compares loss sharpness with seen/unseen class performance.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing the resulting test accuracy with random-example removal.
